brief.headline: Ask for ₹290.00/KG on the Electral sachets (the price we pay Shrinath) and offer to pay in 15 days in exchange for another 5–6% off (roughly their borrowing rate of 10.96%).

priceAsk.summary: Drop the Electral laminate price from ₹295.00/KG to ₹290.00/KG
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Shrinath Roto Pack ₹290.00/KG for the same Electral sachets. The market asking price for pharma ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so our ₹295.00/KG sits at the top of fair. Closing the 1.7% gap to our best price is the floor.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Pay them in 15 days instead of 30 days, in exchange for a 5–6% discount (about ₹12 L/yr)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹9.49 L of our cash, but a 5–6% discount on ₹2.31 Cr saves us about ₹12 L — so we still come out ahead.

brief.financialLeverage: They made a loss of ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25, and their overall health is D (21/100). They also owe 2.15x their own cash (₹208.21 Cr total debt), and their credit rating is IVR BBB- / Stable — all signs they're squeezed for cash. They borrow at about 10.96%, so paying them fast is worth real money. We are only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so they won't risk losing us, but pushing too hard on price alone could tip them over — lead with faster payment for a discount, and keep Huhtamaki or UFLEX ready as a backup.

evidence.point: They made a loss last year
They owe more than twice their own cash
Their health score is very weak
We pay them ₹5/kg more than we pay Shrinath for the same items
We are a tiny part of their business

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (already a tiny FDC supplier) — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets; health C (58/100), revenue ₹2755.75 Cr.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant — both film substrate AND conversion; can second-source at scale; health C (46/100), revenue ₹16492.00 Cr.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter — pharma blister/sachet laminates; strong second-source; health D (31/100), revenue ₹222.04 Cr.

risks: They made a loss (₹-23.68 Cr) and carry high debt (2.15x), with a weak health score (D 21/100) — pushing too hard on price could put steady supply at risk; lead with payment speed and keep a backup live.
They have severe legal cases, GST filing delays, and EPF payment delays on their record — watch for delivery hiccups and don't increase our share of wallet until these clear.
Our ₹2.31 Cr is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we have little volume leverage — the ask must rest on our best-in-house price (₹290.00/KG) and the market band (₹205–305/kg), not on size.

The market asking price (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg) shows we're already at the top of fair at ₹295.00/KG — a cut to ₹290.00/KG is defensible, but going lower needs a different spec or a maker's quote.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to match the ₹290/kg we pay Shrinath on the Electral sachets, and in return we can pay you in 15 days instead of 30 — that's worth about 11% a year to you, so let's split the benefit.
